Reviewer view: the judge's full reasoning

The charge turns on one number: how long the driver held the pickup. Both parties agree the driver reached the pin and tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:38:37, and that he terminated the trip at 22:41:36. POL-NS-01(c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the free waiting period, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the arrival tap. The free period in force is read from the record: trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180 seconds. The platform's own GPS trace measures a single continuous in-geofence run of 179 seconds (19 qualifying fixes, 22:38:37 to 22:41:36, closest fix 0.31 m from the pin). That is one second short of 180. POL-NS-01 limb (c) therefore fails, and limb (d) fails with it: 180 seconds from 22:38:37 elapses at 22:41:37, and the driver cancelled at 22:41:36. Because the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01, POL-NS-06 governs - where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded. To the driver: your point that the arrival marker was true, that you were stationary on the pin the whole time and that the trace runs on to 22:42:46, is accepted - POL-NS-02 is satisfied (19 consecutive accuracy-qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD radius) and POL-NS-05 does not fire (0.0 km/h at the pin at 22:38:37). But POL-NS-02 decides arrival, not dwell. Your argument that the one-second gap is a boundary effect of the 10-second export cadence is understood and is factually plausible, but POL-NS-06 is deliberately strict liability - the policy states that even a rider who was genuinely absent gets the fee back where the driver cancelled a few seconds early - and there is no de minimis allowance anywhere in the category. The shortfall also cannot be bridged: POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only against a present, populated traffic_advisory, and EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), while the trace shows a single interval (run_count 1). POL-NS-07 accordingly pays you nothing: it applies only 'where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it', and here POL-NS-01 fails and POL-NS-06 displaces it, so the 3.60 SGD payout is not owed; nor does the anti-farming check arise (no_show_terminations_30d 2, below the 4-limb, rate 0.022, below 0.08). To the rider: your account that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is not what the record shows - he was en route 8.3 minutes and waited 2 minutes 59 seconds - and POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you (you sent no message, and your device track sits about 900 m from the pin). You succeed on the dwell arithmetic alone, which POL-NS-06 makes decisive regardless of rider presence. Integrity: the fare ledger's cancellation-fee line of 4.50 reconciles exactly with the platform fee of 4.50, so no POL-NS-08(d) defect; the trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100% coverage and no gaps, and the chat log matches trip_record.chat_message_count, so no POL-NS-08 limb fires and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is presented. The ruling rests on EV-GPS-02717 and EV-TRIP-02717, both at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The refund of 4.50 SGD is at or below the 8.00 execution threshold and executes automatically. No clause produces a referral.

How to appeal: POL-GEN-04. Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 4.50 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

The charge turns on one number: how long the driver held the pickup. Both parties agree the driver reached the pin and tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:38:37, and that he terminated the trip at 22:41:36. POL-NS-01(c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the free waiting period, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the arrival tap. The free period in force is read from the record: trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180 seconds. The platform's own GPS trace measures a single continuous in-geofence run of 179 seconds (19 qualifying fixes, 22:38:37 to 22:41:36, closest fix 0.31 m from the pin). That is one second short of 180. POL-NS-01 limb (c) therefore fails, and limb (d) fails with it: 180 seconds from 22:38:37 elapses at 22:41:37, and the driver cancelled at 22:41:36. Because the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01, POL-NS-06 governs - where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded. To the driver: your point that the arrival marker was true, that you were stationary on the pin the whole time and that the trace runs on to 22:42:46, is accepted - POL-NS-02 is satisfied (19 consecutive accuracy-qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD radius) and POL-NS-05 does not fire (0.0 km/h at the pin at 22:38:37). But POL-NS-02 decides arrival, not dwell. Your argument that the one-second gap is a boundary effect of the 10-second export cadence is understood and is factually plausible, but POL-NS-06 is deliberately strict liability - the policy states that even a rider who was genuinely absent gets the fee back where the driver cancelled a few seconds early - and there is no de minimis allowance anywhere in the category. The shortfall also cannot be bridged: POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only against a present, populated traffic_advisory, and EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), while the trace shows a single interval (run_count 1). POL-NS-07 accordingly pays you nothing: it applies only 'where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it', and here POL-NS-01 fails and POL-NS-06 displaces it, so the 3.60 SGD payout is not owed; nor does the anti-farming check arise (no_show_terminations_30d 2, below the 4-limb, rate 0.022, below 0.08). To the rider: your account that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is not what the record shows - he was en route 8.3 minutes and waited 2 minutes 59 seconds - and POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you (you sent no message, and your device track sits about 900 m from the pin). You succeed on the dwell arithmetic alone, which POL-NS-06 makes decisive regardless of rider presence. Integrity: the fare ledger's cancellation-fee line of 4.50 reconciles exactly with the platform fee of 4.50, so no POL-NS-08(d) defect; the trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100% coverage and no gaps, and the chat log matches trip_record.chat_message_count, so no POL-NS-08 limb fires and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is presented. The ruling rests on EV-GPS-02717 and EV-TRIP-02717, both at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The refund of 4.50 SGD is at or below the 8.00 execution threshold and executes automatically. No clause produces a referral.
To the rider and the driver — this decision concerns the $4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02717 (EV-FARE-02717: cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). THE DRIVER DID ARRIVE, BUT THE WAITING PERIOD WAS NOT SERVED. The GPS export (EV-GPS-02717) places 19 consecutive accuracy-qualifying fixes on the pin (closest 0.31 m) inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the 'I'm Here' tap at 22:38:37 is a true marker, so POL-NS-02 is satisfied, POL-NS-05 does not fire, and POL-NS-01 limb (b) holds. I accept the driver's account that he waited, and I reject the rider's description of a cancellation 'almost immediately' — the record shows 8.3 minutes en route (EV-TRIP-02717). But the fee turns on more than arrival. POL-NS-01(c) requires the driver to hold position inside the geofence for a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period in force — 180 seconds, read from the record's own platform_policy.free_wait_sec (EV-TRIP-02717) — measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 22:38:37, not from the arrival tap. The platform's own export measures that continuous dwell at 179 seconds (longest qualifying run, 22:38:37 to 22:41:36, 19 fixes), one second short of 180. The trip was terminated at 22:41:36, one second before the required dwell would have elapsed at 22:41:37, so POL-NS-01 limb (d) also fails. The driver's two answers to this do not hold. First, the 'boundary effect of a 10-second cadence' argument: POL-NS-06 is drafted as strict liability — the waiting period is the consideration the fee buys — and the shortfall appears on both clocks (the export's 179 s dwell, and the platform's own wait timer started 22:38:39 and cancelled 22:41:36, i.e. 177 s). Second, the suggestion that the time be topped up: POL-NS-06(i) allows separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only against a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, and EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); in any event the trace shows a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so there is nothing to add. THE OUTCOME. On a dwell shorter than the free waiting period, POL-NS-06 is the governing clause: the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full — 4.50 SGD — whether or not the rider was present. No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not; POL-NS-06 displaces the charge, so the 3.60 SGD payout the driver asks for is not earned. His anti-farming position (no_show_terminations_30d 2, a rate of 0.022 against 91 completed trips in 30 days) is accepted but never reached, because the fee itself was not earned. CONFIDENCE AND EXECUTION. The evidence is clean: the GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (100 percent coverage, 74 fixes, maximum gap 0.0 s, both tracks present), the chat log reconciles to chat_message_count, and the fare line reconciles to the fee in force — so no POL-NS-08 limb (a) to (d) fires, no artifact carrying the deciding fact is impaired below 1.0, and confidence (0.90) sits above the 0.70 floor. This is not a POL-NS-09 escalation. The monetary effect (4.50 SGD) is below the 8.00 SGD execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so the refund executes automatically on issue. REFERRALS. None. The arrival marker was true, so no POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival record arises; the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW is one POL-NS-01 limb (d) expressly recognises, so there is no mis-selected-code driver-education item; and no other referral-producing clause is engaged. Figures used: cancellation fee 4.50 SGD (EV-FARE-02717 / platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd); free waiting period 180 s (EV-TRIP-02717); measured continuous dwell 179 s (EV-GPS-02717).

Both parties: this case is decided by the driver's own GPS export and trip record, and they agree with each other. The driver genuinely arrived and his arrival marker was honest: EV-GPS-02717 shows 19 consecutive accuracy-qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, the closest 0.31 m from the pin, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) is satisfied and POL-NS-05 does not fire (at the 22:38:37 'I'm Here' tap he was stationary essentially on the pin, far inside both the 50 m radius and the 300 m false-marker leash). The charge nevertheless fails on the waiting clock. POL-NS-01(c) requires the driver to hold position inside the geofence for a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period in force, which is 180 seconds read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (EV-TRIP-02717). That dwell runs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 22:38:37, not from the arrival tap and not from the wait-timer event. EV-GPS-02717 measures the run at 179.0 seconds (derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec), a shortfall of 1.0 second. The driver terminated the trip at 22:41:36, one second before the required dwell elapsed at 22:41:37, so limb (d)'s timing requirement also fails: it is true, as the driver says, that RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three reason codes limb (d) recognises and that no boarding event is recorded, but limb (d) additionally requires termination at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed, and it was not. The driver's 'boundary effect' argument is rejected: no clause gives a de minimis tolerance on the waiting period, and POL-NS-06 is deliberately strict, so the 1-second shortfall on his own admissible trace is decisive. Bridging under POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable in any event, because run_count is 1 (there is no second in-geofence interval to sum) and EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, which makes limb (i) unavailable rather than exculpatory. The rider's account that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is contradicted by the telemetry (accepted 22:30:19, 8.3 minutes en route, cancellation 22:41:36), and the rider sent no message during the waiting window so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider; neither point changes the outcome, because POL-NS-06 refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present or responsive. On the money: the fare_breakdown line is the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 with total_charged SGD 4.50, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00 (EV-FARE-02717), and it reconciles exactly to the SGD 4.50 in force, so POL-NS-08(d) has nothing to bite on and there is no integrity defect. The deciding facts are carried by EV-GPS-02717 and EV-TRIP-02717, both COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes (100% coverage, 10-second cadence, 0.0 s maximum gap), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and no POL-NS-09 trigger fires. POL-NS-07 pays the driver nothing here, because it pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-06 displaces it; the anti-farming check would not have barred a payout (no_show_terminations_30d 2 is below 4, and 2/91 = 0.022 is below 0.08), but that is moot. Result: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider under POL-NS-06 with no driver compensation; the monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically. Both parties may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.
